# A chapter that trips every layer of the gate

She delved into the rich tapestry of the harbour, a testament to the vibrant,
bustling realm nestled between the water and the hill. It was not just a port,
but a promise. The tension was palpable. A wave of something profound washed
over her, and her heart hammered, and her breath hitched, and the air was thick
with salt and with smoke and with the meticulous, seamless weight of the world.

There was something about the counting of it. She began to realise that the
particular kind of quiet in the ledger house was more than a silence — it was a
verdict. Delve, delve, delve went the pen. The myriad coins, the plethora of
crates, the ever-evolving landscape of the debt: a symphony of obligation that
underscored her newfound resolve, showcasing the poignant, evocative, ethereal
nature of the quarter-day.

Not this. Not that. No coin. No crate. No chart. She just very quite really
rather almost somehow suddenly felt it, saw it, watched it, heard it, noticed
it, realised it, seemed to wonder at it — a ghost of a smile, unshed tears,
knuckles white, a shiver down her spine, in the depths of the tapestry of the
realm, a beacon of the way it always was.
